derivation: Written by applying contract/semantics.md to the recorded frames by hand.
NOT generated by running any binding.
Every frame carries ts_str '2026-04/20-13:30:00'. Read as
America/New_York (EDT, UTC-4 on that date) that is 2026-04-20T17:30:00Z,
already minute-aligned so §2.1's flooring is a no-op throughout.
bucket_start then follows §2 and §2.2 per timeframe. EasyLanguage stamps
a bar with its CLOSE, so §2's left label costs one interval before the
grid snap:
Every result is still a grid edge: the intraday grid runs from 09:30 ET
and the offset from that anchor stays divisible in each case.
1d — exempt, and it must be. The daily grid anchors at 04:00 ET (§4)
and alignment discards the time-of-day outright, so 13:30 ET still
first would file the bar under the previous session instead. The
publisher's timestamp is NOT the bucket: EL stamps a daily bar with
the chart's own Date/Time, and it is the binding that aligns.
sid is per-run and was read from this recording. There are no ticks in
this fixture, so nothing else is per-run — every bucket_start above comes
from a hard-coded ts_str.
notes: This fixture is the only end-to-end coverage of the DLL's BarType /
BarInterval -> tf mapping. Without it every recorded frame would be
tf 1m and a regression (say BarInterval 60 mapped to '60m') would reach
a binding before anything noticed.
1d appears TWICE, from BarInterval 0 and BarInterval 1. TradeStation 10
reports 0 on a live daily chart; 1 is what the ABI documented before that
was measured. Both must produce an identical frame apart from seq — the
wire has no way to say which one the chart reported, and must not grow
one.
Three further calls were made and published NOTHING: BarType 1 interval
2 (a 2-minute chart), BarType 3 (weekly), and BarType 2 interval 2 (a
2-day chart). All three returned -5. That is why this fixture has 6
frames from 9 calls. The 2-day case is the subtle one: on BarType 2 the
interval is a day multiplier, so accepting it would put 2-day bars in the
1d partition looking exactly like real daily data.
All six frames carry identical quantities. The harness uses one
intraday-shaped set throughout (el_volume == el_upticks, el_ticks ==
el_upticks + el_downticks); on a real 1d chart EasyLanguage's words mean
something different (semantics.md §3.4), but that is the consumer's table
to read — neither the publisher nor the binding reinterprets them, so the
fixture does not need to model it.
Bars carry no bid/ask in this protocol.
